newsitem.title: BELGIUM: German commitment to cut deficit very clear - Quinn.
newsitem.headline: German commitment to cut deficit very clear - Quinn.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel is "very clear" that Germany will cut its budget deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product this year, Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Monday.
Quinn was speaking in an interview with Reuters Financial Television following talks between EU finance minsters at which Germany and France presented economic convergence programmes.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel "was very clear that Germany would meet, among other things, the Maastricht criteria, specifically the question of the deficit of 2.9 percent," Quinn said, adding that the French and German programmes were "well accepted" by European Union finance ministers.
"He basically said, look we know what we need to do, and what the figure is that we have to achieve," Quinn added.
He noted that Germany had already revised up its forecast for the deficit as a percentage of gross domestic product to 2.9 percent from 2.5 percent.
"They are quite clear in their own minds that that is the outside figure and that they have every intention of meeting it," he added.

Quinn also said that there was wide acceptance that Germany had faced special problems in dealing with German unification in 1990 -- problems which Germany is expected to use to justify a debt to GDP ratio this year which is higher than the 60 percent ceiling suggested in the Maastricht treaty.

"There was broad acceptance that Germany has faced quite unique economic problems. No other country in the world could absorb the cost of unification since 1990 that they have had to absorb," he said.
But ministers also believed that structural reforms now being undertaken in both France and Germany were necessary, Quinn added.
